title: Replace the cabin air filter behind a car's glove box
instruction: Replace the passenger-side cabin air filter element behind the glove box with the new one.
context: Replacing the cabin air filter is routine maintenance for automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023.00; 704,640 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025); on the 2002-2006 Honda CR-V, one of the most common SUVs of its time, its two elements sit behind the glove box. The box only drops once both of its stoppers are squeezed and pushed in; pulling it down past a stopper breaks it.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. The passenger dash of a 2002-2006 Honda CR-V (real trials: its glove box 77500-S9A-A01ZA with stoppers 77547-S9A-G01, and its blower housing with the filter access cover removed and the driver-side element left in its bay) as a fixed grey ABS mock-up, its opening facing the robots: front edge at x 0.32 m, centred on y 0; two side cheeks 12 mm thick, 200 mm deep and 400 mm tall (up to the top panel) with inner faces 366 mm apart, a back wall 400 mm tall and a top panel on it, so the space behind the glove box is reached only through the box's opening. Glove box, tan ABS, 0.55 kg, hinged along its bottom front edge 30 mm above the table at x 0.32: a door 350 mm wide, 270 mm tall and 10 mm thick with a handle, and behind it a bin 350 mm wide, 120 mm deep and 160 mm tall. On each side wall a stopper clip, 3 mm thick, set into the wall's outer face, 20 mm wide, runs from 75 mm up to a tab 35 mm above the wall's top edge, 115 mm behind the hinge, and carries a catch 10 x 10 mm and 6 mm proud, 90 mm up; matching stops on the cheeks catch it and hold the box open at 45 degrees, where it starts, resting on them. Squeezed by its tab and pushed 10 mm into the box (3 N), a stopper clears its stop and stays in. With both in, the box swings down and hangs at 92 degrees. Cabin air filter housing behind it: two trays side by side, each holding one element 112 mm wide and 226 mm deep into the housing. Its access opening, a slot 118 mm wide and 35 mm tall in the back wall, is in front of the passenger-side tray, centred 58 mm right of the centre line; its face is 190 mm behind the hinge and its floor 230 mm above the table; the tray's back stop is 228.5 mm in. The driver-side tray, with its element, sits closed behind the back wall (left in place, not part of the task). Old cabin air filter element, loose, 60 g: one of the CR-V's two elements (Honda 80292-S5D-416, FRAM CF10135), dirty grey-brown pleats in its plastic case, 112 mm wide, 226 mm long and 29 mm thick, in the passenger-side tray with its near end 2 mm inside the slot, with the cartridge's long thin pull tab, 40 mm wide, 20 mm long and 2.5 mm thick, at mid-height on its outer end and a blue airflow mark on its left edge. New element, the same in white, lying flat on a fixed grey stand 120 mm deep, 60 mm wide and 189 mm tall centred at (0.203, -0.47) (right of the dash, all of the element in front of its face), its tab towards the robots and its airflow mark on the left. No other objects.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest. 0 if, at any moment, the box passed through its stops (between 46.5 and 54 degrees open) while either stopper was pushed in less than 4.5 mm: that forces its catch past the stop and breaks it. 0 if the old filter was drawn from its housing (its centre more than 5 mm from where it started), or any of the new filter went into the housing, before the box had passed its stops (opened more than 54 degrees); picking the new filter up beforehand is fine. 0 unless the box passed its stops at some point. Otherwise every positive score needs every fingertip at least 8 cm from the nearest surface of both filters (tabs included) and the box, and every corner of both filters and of the box moved under 1 mm over the last 1 s (21 samples at 20 Hz). Then: 0 unless every part of the old filter, its tab included, is at least 10 mm in front of the housing's slot. 0.25 if it is. 0.5 if also the new filter lies started in its slot: both far corners at least 20 mm inside it, top side up and level within 5 degrees. 1.0 if the new filter is home: its centre within 5 mm of the seated position along the slot, 4 mm across (the tray's 3 mm play a side, plus 1 mm) and 3 mm up, square to the slot and top side up within 3 degrees. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Real trial: synchronized top and side video, with a ruler at the slot face and an angle mark at the hinge, shows the box angle and the stoppers' push-in, the old element's position, the new element's depth (a mark on its visible tab against the slot face locates its rigid body), turn and level, the hands' clearance and the final second's stillness.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Slide the old element back into its bay and put the new one back on its stand; pull both stoppers back out to their catches, swing the box up and let it rest open on them.
fidelity: Rigid bodies and joints in PhysX. Element size is the CR-V's (FRAM CF10135, 112 x 226 x 29 mm; two side by side, each slid in along its long side); its 60 g mass, the glove box, stopper, slot and tray positions are estimates from service guides, not measured. Each stopper is a rigid clip on a 3 N spring that latches once pushed 7 mm in; a forced stop is scored, not broken. The access cover starts removed; the driver-side element stays in its tray.
